faq.question: Q1. What is the last date to apply for the PGIMER Data Entry Operator recruitment?
faq.answer: The last date to submit the application for the PGIMER Data Entry Operator recruitment is 27th August 2026.

faq.question: Q2. What is the educational qualification required for the Data Entry Operator post?
faq.answer: Candidates must hold a Graduation degree from a recognized University and possess knowledge of data entry work with a speed of at least 8000 key depressions per hour.

faq.question: Q3. What is the age limit for the Data Entry Operator position?
faq.answer: The maximum age limit for the Data Entry Operator post is 30 years. Age relaxation will be provided as per Government of India rules.

faq.question: Q4. What is the salary offered for the Data Entry Operator role?
faq.answer: The selected candidate will receive a consolidated salary of Rs. 20,000 per month.

faq.question: Q5. Is there any application fee for this recruitment?
faq.answer: No, there is no application fee mentioned for any category (General/OBC, SC/ST) for this recruitment.

faq.question: Q6. What is the selection process for the Data Entry Operator posts?
faq.answer: The selection process will involve a Written Test and a Typing Test.

faq.question: Q7. How can I apply for the PGIMER Data Entry Operator recruitment?
faq.answer: The application process is offline. Candidates need to download the application form, fill it correctly, attach necessary documents, and send it to the official address mentioned in the notification before the last date.

faq.question: Q8. What is the contract period for this position?
faq.answer: The contract period for the Data Entry Operator position is until 31st March 2027.

faq.question: Q9. Where can I find the official notification and application form?
faq.answer: The official notification and application form can be accessed through the PGIMER official website, www.pgimer.edu.in. Links are provided in the Important Links section.

faq.question: Q10. Is this a permanent government job?
faq.answer: No, this is a contractual position.
